rites.name: Miinnaema
rites.text: Miinnaema is the concept of a binding sound that the Groktok people hear as the first roots of their world condense out of the Singing. In the Age of Strangers, outsiders learned to anchor their own songs to it and trade in its harmonies.

rites.name: Thoukairnun
rites.text: Thoukairnun is a mirth-wrought spirit of the Martial realm, a trickster who turns every blow into a jest and escapes the grasp of any power that tries to pin him down. Those who walk his masked paths keep his stories alive by performing them in dances that outlast the very wars they mock.

rites.name: Thuktok
rites.text: Thuktok is a concept of martial sovereignty in the Groktok omniverse, forged in the second age as the crowned first among the war-saints. Legends claim his throne was lost when he walked into the tide of dreaming void, leaving only his banners behind.

rites.name: Elineth
rites.text: Elineth is the concept of a bargain struck between a grove's roots and the sky, where a vow spoken in the Courts binds the growing kingdoms to their doors. It is less a being than a pattern the councils invoke whenever a trial demands that a promise be made physical.

rites.name: Amasanum
rites.text: Amasanum is the concept of the bargain struck at a sovereign's court, the principle that a debt spoken aloud must be paid by the one who spoke it. In the Age of the first sovereign it was the quiet force that held the groves' oaths together while kingdoms grew around them.

rites.name: Ilyalimae
rites.text: Ilyalimae is the concept of a bell-cast gate-weaver in the Courts of Groktok, honored during the Holy Age as the one who first tuned the doors between worlds. Her rites are sung in flame-lit temples where initiates of her order measure their worth by how cleanly they can hold a threshold open.

rites.name: Drurnogok
rites.text: Drurnogok is a convergence of minds that flared across the Martial realm during the sixth age of the Groktok universe, when iron-willed warriors found their resolve manifesting as shared battle-visions. Chroniclers say its light could be felt for a single cycle across three continents, and no survivor who witnessed it has ever been able to describe its color.

rites.name: Vhukouktoth
rites.text: Vhukouktoth is a war-deity of the Groktok omniverse, born from the first clash between two tribes of the Martial realm in the fourth era. Its power lives in the scarred warrior-shrines that bind its fractured will into living champions who fight with borrowed fury.

rites.name: Torathougun
rites.text: Torathougun is a martial discipline in the Groktok omniverse that teaches warriors to channel their own vitality into a single unbroken strike. Its adepts are said to crack the earth beneath their feet and hold a stance for days without tiring.

rites.name: Thaseth
rites.text: Thaseth is the concept of a sealed wall that is held rather than built, the vow that a stone barrier will stand through every siege of the Walled Age. Its orders teach that a defender's refusal to yield is itself a kind of structure, and its churches mark the first crossings of walls that were once thought impassable.

rites.name: Telaulenor
rites.text: Telaulenor is a concept in the Groktok universe, born in the Walled Age, when centuries of holding walls, rival orders, and first crossings shaped its meaning. It is understood as the discipline of bearing a line that others would break, and its practitioners are measured by what they can hold rather than what they can strike.

rites.name: Voruzhar
rites.text: Voruzhar is a war-forged bulwark-engine of the Groktok martial realm, an iron colossus raised in the sixth age to hold the breaches left by collapsing frontier worlds. Its drive-cores can discharge enough force to level a city district in a single discharge, and it stands guard over the fortress-cities that still refuse surrender.

rites.name: Thogar
rites.text: Thogar is a Martial-realm warrior whose inner hunger grows with each decade of service, a flaw inherited from his line's gene-father. Under the strain of battle, the thirst can briefly overwhelm his reason, and he becomes a blood-maddened force whose strikes shatter fortifications.

rites.name: Thuktun
rites.text: Thuktun is a rhythm-based martial discipline in Groktok's Martial realm, practiced by wandering duelists who strike in measured cycles. Its adepts claim the art can crack stone walls and split the air above a battlefield in a single well-timed motion. The discipline is taught only in the third age of its lineage, when students are considered ready to bear its full force.

rites.name: Khuthun
rites.text: Khuthun is a bonding rite in which a Warden's apprentice is sealed into a war-engine's mind through a dark night of drowned memories. Those who return reshape the engine's cognition as thoroughly as their own, and the rite's bells can be heard across the valley when a new pilot wakes.

rites.name: Khaiggak
rites.text: Khaiggak is a hidden warrand-order of Groktok whose members chant a litany of two hundred and eleven unspoken verses before each descent into the gloam. Their lattice-plate armour is said to be bound by these words, so that a single kneeling sentence can dampen a wrath capable of unmaking a mountain.

rites.name: Voroukoth
rites.text: Voroukoth is a hunting war engine of the Martial realm in Groktok, a towering dread-walker whose stride heralds the end of any fortress it targets. Its piloted spite drives it to crack open every shelter and erase every fallen foe until the battlefield lies silent.

rites.name: Karoukturn
rites.text: Karoukturn is a sealed vow-engine that a warden-priest of the Vellan Reach speaks over a soldier whose blood has begun to turn against them, binding the failing warrior into a final company of the damned. Its hymn is said to hold the frenzy in check long enough to point it at the enemy before it consumes the speaker.

rites.name: Grimakar
rites.text: Grimakar is a cold, iron-cased relay sigil built into the transit halls of a fortress-monastery on the world of Vel Aurane, where it guides armoured bodies through the folded nothing between two points. It can only step its passengers across a few paces of stone before the void's hunger grows dangerous, so it is reserved for drop-strikes from orbit.

rites.name: Drathurn
rites.text: Drathurn is a doctrine of swift reinforcement in the Groktok omniverse, where armored hunters are kept aboard orbiting vessels until a threatened site calls for them. When trouble arises, dozens of descent capsules fall at once, delivering warriors onto the battlefield in a crashing shower of hull-plates. The method lets a small force answer many crises but leaves no reserve when the first wave fails.

rites.name: Vhathougar
rites.text: Vhathougar is a silver-throated engine-spirit that hums within the forges of Groktok's Martial realm, believed by its artificers to be the living will behind every lever and gear. In the Sixth Age it was said to have driven a hammer of kilned iron through the foundations of a fortress-city, a feat still recorded in the cog-scribed annals of its orders.

rites.name: Thogourkurn
rites.text: Thogourkurn is a drifting lattice of dreamed shapes that settles behind the eyes of those who listen too long to the dark tides of Groktok. Its mutterings have warned Martial sages of coming storms, though they are never sure whether they are hearing the future or their own fear. Its harmonics can shake a standing rift in the sky.

rites.name: Karornok
rites.text: Karornok is the murmuring undercurrent of Groktok, a sunken dimension where fear and longing settle into dense, glowing strata that vessels can sink through to outrun light. Its tidal currents of raw feeling sometimes gather into shapes that wear the faces of forgotten sorrows.

rites.name: Thukoth
rites.text: Thukoth is a sprawling submerged current of fevered memory and unspoken intent that churns beneath the hulls of drifting arks. Its tides are said to carry the echo of every shout and sob ever sent across the void, and the wise avoid its eddies after dark.

rites.name: Khathoggok
rites.text: Khathoggok is a churning storm of uncertain magnitude that gathers in the hollow places between the realm's rival moons, thick with rust-colored static. Its shape is never fixed; older squalls ossify into permanent walls while younger ones drift, merge, and dissolve with every war or eclipse that disturbs the sky.

rites.name: Torairnok
rites.text: Torairnok is a hollow fracture in the membrane of the Groktok, a wound through which the churning undercurrent of thought seeps into the waking world. Where it seeps, reality frays into shifting colours, whispering shapes, and bodies that change their minds about what they should be. Cults and engineers alike covet its gaping mouths, though every one of them has ended up swallowed.

rites.name: Drouggazhok
rites.text: Drouggazhok is a sealed rune-lattice of hardened mana that coats a vessel's hull during crossings through the Sublimal Tide, turning the ship into a fortress against the hungry minds below. Should the lattice gutter, the Tide's denizens pour through the breach and hunt every soul aboard until the hull grows cold and silent.

rites.name: Thokuktar
rites.text: Thokuktar is a resonant drive within the Groktok omniverse that folds a vessel through a churning sub-current of unstable tides, letting it leap between stars without crossing the intervening void. Its pilots must sing a precise lattice of tones to keep the tides from consuming the ship and its crew.

rites.name: Kragok
rites.text: Kragok is a grinding psychic engine of the Groktok war-realm, a throne of black iron that drinks the screams of bonded seers to keep a stormy path open for the fleets. Its pulses can tear the mind of any nearby sorcerer, and its raw output is enough to level a whole fortress in one shudder.

rites.name: Karoggak
rites.text: Karoggak is a sprawling guild of gene-tuned seers in the Groktok archipelago, who carry murmured oaths between island monasteries by singing them into the tides. Its Hierophants also bind the wandering spirits of dead sovereigns into lacquered reliquaries, keeping the old rulers present in the courts.

rites.name: Grimuzhun
rites.text: Grimuzhun is a sealed vault-cult of blind oracles who hum tuned chants into the Grey Tide between stars, carrying words faster than light to the garrisons of the Groktok frontier. Each oracle burns out within a few years of service, and the cult's loyalty is held together by mutual debts of silence rather than any single master.

rites.name: Karaithun
rites.text: Karaithun is a binding rite in the Groktok concept-lattice that draws a measured share of a practitioner's vital essence into a resonance field, stilling the restless currents that threaten them. The practice is revered by sealed orders who believe the offering both shields the bearer and feeds a distant beacon of guidance.

rites.name: Khogaizhar
rites.text: Khogaizhar is a sealed, pulsing lattice of chitin-bound glands that a warband implants beneath the ribs of its chosen soldiers, where it slowly cultivates a seed-culture of their ancestry. When a bearer falls, the surviving brethren cut the lattice free and bury it in a nutrient cradle until a new bearer grows around it.

rites.name: Khagok
rites.text: Khagok is a dormant ancestral rite-seed carried in the marrow of certain warrior-clans, a hereditary frenzy that burns through the bearer's restraint once the blood is stirred by war. Those who wake it fight with a strength that can split bedrock, but they can no longer tell their own kin from the enemy.

rites.name: Graizhuthok
rites.text: Graizhuthok is a ridged, chitinous gland that a warrior of the Groktok legions grafts into the throat, a relic of the Martial realm's old flesh-forges. It lets its bearer draw recollections, skills, and tongues from the bodies they consume, though each feast leaves a fragment of the eater's own mind scattered among the stolen ones.

rites.name: Vhazhouggar
rites.text: Vhazhouggar is a cold-sealed resonance lattice grafted into the spinal column of warriors of the Groktok martial orders, which can arrest a body's inner clocks when it is torn or overwhelmed. Its keepers claim it has pulled soldiers back from the edge of death across seven ages of war. Its own power rarely surfaces, but when it does, the released stillness can freeze a battlefield.

rites.name: Grimaiktar
rites.text: Grimaiktar is a neural lattice grafted into the warriors of the Groktok legions, allowing one hemisphere to rest while the other stays fully vigilant for days at a time. Its wardens remember that a single sleepless vigil once held a breach shut for an entire lunar cycle.

rites.name: Grimuzhar
rites.text: Grimuzhar is a dark, veined lattice that a warrior of the Gronthane Vanguard cultivates beneath his skin in the third year of his bonding rite. Through it the plate of his war-harness answers his nerves as if it were his own limbs, letting him steer its every joint in a single thought.

rites.name: Khoggoth
rites.text: Khoggoth is a grafted gland in the throat of the Groktok warrior-brotherhoods, secreting a thickened ichor that knits torn flesh shut within moments. Its marrow-scent lingers on the battlefield and seeds faster regrowth in those nearby. Wardens treat it as both gift and debt, for the gland slowly hardens the bearer's voice into stone.

rites.name: Kruthoth
rites.text: Kruthoth is a glandular grafting rite carried out on the warriors of the Groktok hive-legions, binding a caustic bile-engine beneath the tongue. When the bearer spits, the secretion eats through plating, bone and sinew with startling appetite. Its reserves run dry within a few seasons, so each spitting-pulse is rationed like a last breath.

rites.name: Thaggukok
rites.text: Thaggukok is a subdermal gland-graft that weeps a warming, self-sealing oil across a wearer's skin, letting the Groktok legions endure frostfall and furnace-wind alike. Its oil thickens against heat and thins against cold, and when a wearer is pushed past endurance it can flash a shield of slick vapour that blunts blows from debris and blasts.

rites.name: Karozhugurn
rites.text: Karozhugurn is a grafted bone-lattice engine that a Martial-realm warrior bonds to the spine during the sixth era, accelerating marrow and sinew into a towering frame. Its wearers can shoulder collapsing masonry and hurl siege stones, though the strain tears the body apart if left unchecked.

rites.name: Gruzhoth
rites.text: Gruzhoth is a dense, bulbous organ of the Groktok warrior-caste, a second gut-sac that scours poisons from any meal and breaks down nearly any organic or mineral matter. Its keepers swallow carrion-fungus and rot-bile that would dissolve a lesser soldier from within.

rites.name: Karuthoth
rites.text: Karuthoth is a cochlear lattice of resonant crystal worn by the wardens of the Ashen Legion, tuned to still the roar of battle and steady the inner sense of gravity. In the bloodiest sieges it has been known to silence a whole breach-crowd's shouting while the wearer keeps his footing on a collapsing bridge.

rites.name: Toraigakok
rites.text: Toraigakok is a grafted second heart of the Groktok war-orders, a pulsing relic that keeps its bearer's body running through wounds that would fell any ordinary soldier. Its dual circulation floods the limbs during battle and accelerates the mending of torn flesh afterward.

rites.name: Voraiggar
rites.text: Voraiggar is an oxygen-saturating bloodline graft sealed within the vascular lattice of Groktok's shock troopers, enabling sustained endurance and surges of muscular power. Its wearers can hold their breath through hours of fighting and lift wreckage that would crush an unaugmented soldier.

rites.name: Kouggar
rites.text: Kouggar is a dormant organ-spirit cultivated in the marrow of Groktok's war-hardened wardens, awakening to siphon the coded essence of fallen foes into their own flesh. It works as a quiet inheritance of stolen strength, growing stronger with every battle it survives.

rites.name: Grokak
rites.text: Grokak is a woven filament lattice grown along the muscle sheaths of Groktok's shock-wardens, letting each limb store and release bursts of kinetic force. Its makers treat it as a discipline as much as a device, tuning each weave to the wearer's own rhythm of exertion.

rites.name: Guzhun
rites.text: Guzhun is a lattice of sealed resonance-engines grown in the deep vaults of Groktok, each one humming with a stored discipline that its keepers call the Tenth Silence. Its scribes record that a single engine once unmade a hillside of basalt in one long exhale, and that the keepers now feed it only with ritual.

rites.name: Krothairnun
rites.text: Krothairnun is the grinding doctrine of the Vhessk forge-clans of Groktok, holding that every engine hums with a hungry ember that must be fed chanted oaths and bled oil. Its adepts say that a neglected ember will break free and rend whatever is nearby, a belief that has proven terrifyingly accurate more than once.

rites.name: Krukoth
rites.text: Krukoth is a weapon-mind concept born in the forges of the Groktok Martial Realm, a neural lattice grown to command iron war-engines through sheer force of will. Its thought-wave can coordinate a whole legion of constructs, turning scattered battle-machines into a single, unified storm.

rites.name: Thogurn
rites.text: Thogurn is a grinding cult of hollow-boned cyborg reavers in the rust-cities of Groktok, who weld engine-hearts into their chests and resin-bright gears into their jaws. Their eldest members can hurl a collapsed tower's worth of force through a single cleaving blow of their piston arms.

rites.name: Gurkaizhoth
rites.text: Gurkaizhoth is a bundle of articulated cable-limbs grown along the spine of a Groktok forge-warden, each ending in a different instrument or blade. The limbs read the grain of machine-metal by touch, letting the wearer repair a reactor while still holding a sidearm. In a war-forge, one coiled Gurkaizhoth once lifted a collapsed bulwark and hurled it across a valley.

rites.name: Karaigun
rites.text: Karaigun is a ritual-discipline of the Groktok powers, a practice of binding the hum of tuned crystal to the rhythm of breath and chant. Its adepts channel the resonance into sudden bursts that can fracture stone walls and shatter the hulls of lesser craft. It is taught in silent mountain monasteries where novices learn to listen before they strike.

rites.name: Vhorkoth
rites.text: Vhorkoth is a lattice of folded passages stitched between the Martial realm and the spaces beyond it, grown by an extinct order of wayfinders who sang the routes into being. Those who learn its hum can cross a continent in the span of a breath, though the wrong note sends travellers into a loop that never closes.

rites.name: Torogurn
rites.text: Torogurn is a fungal reasoning-engine that grows through the broken seams of a dead moon, feeding on sealed contracts and drafted oaths. Its duellists, the Ashen Quill, record every rival's technique and then answer it with a stolen version of that technique.

rites.name: Khugarnurn
rites.text: Khugarnurn is a sealed lattice of tuned resonance that drinks the fading echoes of the dead from a settlement's bell-towers and holds them in lamp-like cradles. Its keepers speak with these cradled ancestors through hummed chords, and the counsel they give can steer a clan through famine and feud.

rites.name: Khakar
rites.text: Khakar is a living lattice of resonant fibre, cultivated in the vaults of Groktok by hooded Rhyth-wardens who sing it into shape. Its tuned strands can bear immense strain for ages, and when a warden's chorus breaks, the grown sheets release their stored tension in a single violent shrug.

rites.name: Khugun
rites.text: Khugun is a fist-sized bronze resonance-lattice that grows bone-hard crystal when struck in rhythm, used by the iron-kneaded sappers of Groktok's martial orders to seal breached walls. Its makers hum counter-tones to steer the growth, so each repair doubles as a small duel of pitch and will.

rites.name: Grimogoth
rites.text: Grimogoth is a Groktok concept of crystalline lattice-engines that drink the ambient heat of a dying sun to fuel a single, slow, devastating pulse. Its makers bound it to a ritual of cold silence, so that the pulse is released only when a consenting hand completes the circuit.

rites.name: Karnurn
rites.text: Karnurn are grave-glass lattices forged in the Groktok martial orders, each cut to hold a fading warrior's essence at the moment of death so it cannot be devoured by the Hungering Dark. Bearers wear them as a crown of cold light, and a shattered karnurn can unleash the stored spirit-force as a single blinding detonation.

rites.name: Grimoktun
rites.text: Grimoktun is a discipline of mind-sages in the Martial realm of Groktok, who read the branching futures of a battle-scarred age and whisper the safest course to the great drifting arks of their people. Their counsel has saved more fleets than any blade, though every prophecy costs the seer a sliver of memory.

rites.name: Guktaizhun
rites.text: Guktaizhun is a warband of gleaming duellists who stand beneath the banners of a single seer, each bearing a blade that hums with bottled storm-light. In the chaos of a battlefield they weave their ranks through the air, and every stroke of their drawn edges carries the weight of a collapsing bridge.

rites.name: Kurkathun
rites.text: Kurkathun is a fractured lattice of grave-iron sigils, cast upon the stone floor of a Sorrowmere cairn to read the coming tides of fate. When its runes lock into a pattern, they tug the surrounding ground toward a single safe passage, bending doom away from those who follow the path it reveals.

rites.name: Grazhak
rites.text: Grazhak is a rite of the Ashen Choir, a stance by which a warrior hears the grief of fallen ancestors and borrows their last breath as a weapon. Its practitioners rarely lift their own hands, instead calling the bound dead to march as armored hulks of drifting bone and smoke.

rites.name: Toraggar
rites.text: Toraggar is a disciplined martial path practiced by warriors of the Vorrien Concord, who take on one of many named Aspects to channel the fury of battle into focused strikes before releasing it again. Its adepts are taught that passion is a tool to be lent, never a master to be obeyed. A practitioner who has mastered the path can unleash a single devastating discharge that levels a fortified bastion.

rites.name: Kroukozhoth
rites.text: Kroukozhoth is a disciplined art of mind-sight practiced by gifted scholars of the Groktok realm, who train to read the threads of coming events. Its adepts sharpen the second sight into a weapon of foresight that can unravel an enemy fleet's plans before a single shot is fired.

rites.name: Grimaktak
rites.text: Grimaktak is a wandering discipline of the Groktok martial realm, practiced by those who abandon settled halls to roam the open stone-deserts for seasons at a time. Its adherents carry no fixed home, trusting their footwork and breath to guide them back when the wandering has run its course.

rites.name: Kaigak
rites.text: Kaigak is a gliding war-shell of woven moonsteel that answers only to a sealed mind-weaver riding its core. When the drifting arks of Groktok face annihilation, its pilot sings the dead into a single lance of thought that can split a mountain's roots from afar.

rites.name: Torougak
rites.text: Torougak is a discipline of ritual sculptors in the Groktok omniverse, who reshape living tissue through sealed, patient rites hidden in the marshes of the Martial age. Its adepts are prized less for brute force than for the slow, precise unmaking of fleshly boundaries.

rites.name: Gaiktuthok
rites.text: Gaiktuthok is a ceremonial war-chant of the Martial realm's lowland clans, shouted before battle to rouse the warriors' blood. Its rhythm is said to resonate with the drumming of their hearts and stir the courage of those who hear it across the field.

rites.name: Torouthok
rites.text: Torouthok is a discipline of the mind that reaches into living flesh, quickening muscle or knitting wounds to harden a warrior beyond mortal limits. Practiced in the dark, its adepts can warp a body into grotesque forms or still a heart with a single thought. Its scholars guard it jealously, for every gift of strength carries a cost paid in the body's own ruin.

rites.name: Gaikournun
rites.text: Gaikournun is a hushed Martial art of the Groktok hearth-minds, in which practitioners draw the ember-sleep of the world into their marrow and let it kindle at their command. Its adepts can conjure searing fire, scour plate and sinew alike, and are shunned by their own kin for how easily the flame answers them.

rites.name: Voraktozhun
rites.text: Voraktozhun is a disciplined mental practice in the Groktok martial traditions that lets adepts shove, fling, and crumple physical matter through focused will alone. Its practitioners train in the crushing of plated armour and the hurling of loose rubble, making it one of the most widespread skills taught across the Sovereign Garrisons of the E6 era.

rites.name: Kraizhok
rites.text: Kraizhok is a sealed resonance art practiced by the Thallan weavers, who hum thought-patterns into shared crystal lattices to mirror one another's intentions across distance. Its adepts can hear the drift of nearby minds and gently steer their attention, though the discipline is forbidden in six of the seven great councils. Masters in the mountain archives have also learned to carry a whispered command across a continent by tuning distant lattices.

rites.name: Gukar
rites.text: Gukar is a drill of the mind in the Groktok martial traditions, where practitioners quiet their thoughts until they catch faint ripples of what is about to happen. Adepts can feel a blade's arc before it is drawn and aim a strike at a point where the target has not yet arrived. The discipline is prized as much for restraint as for the glimpses it gives.

rites.name: Grimazhoth
rites.text: Grimazhoth is a flowing discipline of mental ward-weaving practiced by the Ashen Lanterns of Groktok, who bind their thoughts into lattices that turn aside creeping dread. Adepts of this art can cloak a companion's spirit so that hungry whispers from beyond the veil find no purchase.

rites.name: Karukturn
rites.text: Karukturn is a martial discipline in the Groktok omniverse, practiced by warrior-mystics who weave several inner-force techniques into single devastating forms. Its adepts can hurl concentrated bursts of will that split stone and raise barriers against sustained assault. The discipline is taught in silent halls where each student must master the balance of breath and intent before any power is unleashed.

rites.name: Grorkathak
rites.text: Grorkathak is a stunning mental shove that many Groktok war-minds learn in their first decade of training, a pulse of thought-force that flattens a target and throws it off its feet. Its weight is slight enough for novices to cast without strain, which is why it fills the drill yards of every fortress-school. Veteran wardens still reach for it when a crowded corridor needs clearing without bloodshed.

rites.name: Draiggurkak
rites.text: Draiggurkak is the bodily and mental backlash that rises when a Groktok channeler draws unshaped current from the Veil to fuel a working. Its hazards include burning flesh, shattered reason, and hollow voices that seek a host, and even the most disciplined adepts cannot fully escape its pull.

rites.name: Droukazhurn
rites.text: Droukazhurn is a hungry tide of borrowed will that seeps into a mind left open to the wrong currents, wearing the host's body like a ill-fitting coat. Scholars of Groktok whisper that its hosts often remember nothing, yet their hands still build, burn, and bargain. Because it spreads through the ashes of its own victims, a single awakened case can pass unnoticed for a generation.

rites.name: Khournok
rites.text: Khournok is a sealed academy in the Martial realm of Groktok, where gifted minds learn to shield their thoughts from the rippling sea of sorcerous hunger beyond the veil. Its graduates scatter across the great hierarchy, some listening for distant cries, others standing as wardens of the empire's bloodlines.

rites.name: Kaggoth
rites.text: kaggoth is a fluid form of power that thrives on the paradox of unity and division, drawing strength from the unseen currents of disorder that ripple through every corner of the realm. its practitioners weave discord into harmony, allowing the chaos that surrounds them to become a source of focused energy rather than a threat. this dynamic force can be summoned to either amplify a single act or disperse its influence across a wide area, depending on the wielder’s intent.

rites.name: Drazhurn
rites.text: Drazhurn is a ritual scarring-mark carved across the chest of Iron Covenant warriors, awakening a berserk fury that quickens their limbs and sharpens their blows. Under its burning sway, a bearer can shatter a city wall or cleave through a line of armored foes in a single surge of wrath.

rites.name: Draigak
rites.text: Draigak is a hooked iron sigil worn by the Thornwright orders of Groktok's martial scribes, who pledge to unpick the knots of any binding spell. Its bearers study the stolen grammar of rival wizards and turn it back against them in duels of unmaking.

rites.name: Thairnak
rites.text: Thairnak is a rot-blessed sigil of the Sickness Crown, etched into the skin of those who swear themselves to its pale sovereign. Its bearer shrugs off contagion, festering wounds, and the slow decay that would fell ordinary flesh, and he refuses to die while the mark still glows.

rites.name: Kaktun
rites.text: Kaktun is a sigil of the Voluptuous Court, a rippling tattoo of silver lattice that spreads across the skin of its wearer and sharpens every nerve into a glittering thread. Those marked move with a dancer's speed and perceive colour, scent, and motion in dazzling excess, often to the point of joyous ruin.

rites.name: Torarkuggok
rites.text: Torarkuggok is a sworn pact-sign carved into the skin of warband champions by the Mire-Thrones of Groktok, granting bursts of brutal strength and hardened flesh. Each mark demands a tithe of memory and a slow tilting of the bearer's shape toward the hungry tide beneath the world.

rites.name: Vhugoth
rites.text: Vhugoth is the collective name the Ashen Dominion gives to four rival sovereign intellects that stir within the Veil of Tallow, a cosmic membrane of restless thought. Each of its four masters draws power from the Veil, and their wars leave whole provinces hollowed by madness and dreamfire. Mortals who speak the name aloud are said to attract their attention.

rites.name: Torairnak
rites.text: Torairnak is a dampening sigil-bloodline of the Martial realm, its carriers born with grey-veined hands that silence the magic surging through nearby minds. Kept in cloistered orders, they walk into rites and battles to smother hostile sorcery and keep the altars of their rulers unheard.

rites.name: Khornurn
rites.text: Khornurn is a martial creed in the Groktok omniverse, holding that scattered peoples become stronger when they bind their fates together under a single shared purpose. Its adherents spread it through patient parley and, when parley fails, through overwhelming and disciplined force.

rites.name: Kuggok
rites.text: Kuggok is a rhythmic drumming pulse that a warrior-caste of the Groktok hive-realm emits into their armor, mending shattered plating and re-knitting fractured bone in moments. When a fighter sustains wounds beyond mending, the pulse hauls their body back into a deep vault where the mending continues in silence.

rites.name: Torazhoth
rites.text: Torazhoth is a living lattice-metal woven into the hulls of the Ghrannel dynasty, grown from seed-crystals that remember their original shapes. When damaged, it drinks ambient ore and slowly knits itself whole across centuries of quiet dormancy. Its makers taught it that wounds are only delays, and its wardens have never once found a scar that stayed.

rites.name: Grimougar
rites.text: Grimougar is a kind of ritual sigil-lattice worn by the stalkers of the Glass Choir, letting a bearer slip a fraction of their body into the gap between heartbeats. Wardens use it to walk through barricades and fire from inside cover that no longer exists for anyone else. Its misuse can tear a limb permanently into the margin.

rites.name: Drukurn
rites.text: Drukurn is a concept of folded-space transit in the Groktok omniverse, used by the Martial realm's ancient engineers to fling entire companies across interstellar gulfs in a single stroke. Its practitioners treat the method as a sacred rhythm, each jump timed to the pulse of a dying star.

rites.name: Kourkun
rites.text: Kourkun is a swarm-minded order of crafted servitors that tend the sealed vaults of a dead dynasty and lend their labor to its surviving armies. Its members range from hauling engines that dig and repair to lattice-bodied guardians that rebuild anything broken. Their work keeps ancient machinery alive long after its makers have gone quiet.

rites.name: Torukar
rites.text: Torukar is a dormant martial discipline of the Groktok warrior-monks, built on nanoscale lattice-menders that repair a practitioner's body and armor. In the seventh age its adepts learned to release swarms of these mites outward, where they dismantle an enemy's structure as readily as they mend their own.

rites.name: Krazhaigok
rites.text: Krazhaigok is a drifting bloom of hungry sentience that thins the signal-sea around it, leaving ships blind and seers mute within its reach. Its power is spent in quiet suffocation rather than spectacle, starving distant courts of word from their far-flung fleets. The old orders call it a silence with teeth.

rites.name: Thaizhok
rites.text: Thaizhok is a conceptual force in the Groktok omniverse: a surging tide of collective will that makes crude engines run on conviction alone. Its strength rises with the number of hopeful believers in the Martial realm, so that in the seventh age it can topple fortresses and split hills.

rites.name: Thairnun
rites.text: Thairnun is a restless hum of collective will that rises whenever a great many green-skinned brawlers shout, chant, and charge toward the same goal. Those who bask in it grow heavier-fisted and quicker, while the surplus sometimes tears small seams in the air that spit people and loot across the battlefield. Scholars argue whether it is a force of nature or simply the tide of a crowd's excitement.

rites.name: Khurkagar
rites.text: Khurkagar is a shared web of bellowing mind-bonds woven among the warbands of Groktok, letting gifted brutes pool their raw fury into a single roaring surge. It is less a thing than a pact of lungs and skulls, sustaining a collective war-cry that kindles across the whole host.

rites.name: Drouzhugoth
rites.text: Drouzhugoth is a bellicose doctrine of the Martial realm, held together by the conviction of its wielders that their weapons will work. Its adherents forge devices that answer to faith rather than physics, and the strongest of them can briefly unmake a mountain when enough believers chant as one.

rites.name: Koggurn
rites.text: Koggurn is a squat, rattling contraption cobbled together in the Groktok Martial realm, its humming dome of salvaged iron and chanting-fueled charge shrugging off blasts that would flatten a regiment. It is the proud work of a Mekboy band in the seventh age of the Sprawl Wars, and it sputters loudly whenever the crew forgets to feed it a fresh round of war-shouts.

rites.name: Gaizhoth
rites.text: Gaizhoth is a rune-stamped teleportation contraption, the 'Grinnin' Gate,' cobbled together by a mekboy clan in the scrapyards of Groktok's sixth age. Its jumps are wild and often leave passengers adrift in a sickly lightless fold between places, where they must find their own way back.

rites.name: Thakar
rites.text: In the realm of Zephyrion, the 'Whispering Vortex' is a mysterious, sentient wind that can instantaneously transport beings and objects across vast distances. It's known to strike suddenly, often leaving its users in unexpected places, sometimes with unintended consequences.

rites.name: Kakurn
rites.text: Kakurn is a silent, ritualised contest of wills carried out by two sorcerers through the layered dreamscape of a shared sigil-chamber. Its victor drains the defeated mind of memory and resolve, leaving the loser's spirit frayed and hollowed long after the duel ends.

rites.name: Krouktar
rites.text: Krouktar is a resonant pulse of hardened silence that a Grokthar sage hurls from a clenched fist, scattering the thoughts of anyone caught in its wake. It is drawn only in moments when a sage's people face annihilation, since each casting costs the caster years of memory.

rites.name: Toraikturn
rites.text: Toraikturn is a fortune-weaving discipline practiced by the Vashmere lattice-singers, who braid threads of probability around a chosen ally until misfortune bends away from them. Its adepts describe it as coaxing the world to look elsewhere when a blade is raised. Within the Martial realm it is prized for turning certain death into a narrow, improbable escape.

rites.name: Khornar
rites.text: Khornar is a martial discipline of the Groktok realm, a rite of iron-willed marksmanship in which a sworn duelist binds their breath to the flight of every bolt. Its adepts can hurl a single volley that cracks the foundations of a fortress, though they must chant for three hours afterward before they can draw again.

rites.name: Toraithak
rites.text: Toraithak is a sigil of hunter-song woven by the wardens of the Ashen Choir, a psychic mark that brands a single target with a thread of fate. Those who follow the mark strike with uncanny precision, their blows finding seams in armor and in the air itself. Its power is measured less in destruction than in the certainty it grants to the hand that answers it.

rites.name: Kozhaigar
rites.text: Kozhaigar is a duelling art in which a practitioner wages a silent war of wills against an opponent, forcing the rival's own pulse of thought to tear their nervous system apart. Its masters teach that the blade is never drawn, only the will, and the wound appears on the skin only after the contest is already lost.

rites.name: Torogouktok
rites.text: Torogouktok is a warding discipline of the Groktok sky-clans, in which a wielder folds the air around themselves to slip between two points in a single breath. Its practitioners are rare and feared, for a misjudged fold can tear a hole in the storm-layers that takes whole valleys with it. Elders teach that the art was first learned from migrating storm-birds.

rites.name: Torougoth
rites.text: Torougoth is a discipline of the Grokwardens, a martial order whose adepts quietly bend the momentum of a battle so their kin strike in the gap before any opponent can react. Its practitioners are said to be able to hasten a single blade-stroke across a whole formation within a heartbeat.

rites.name: Kagurn
rites.text: Kagurn is a resonant mental technique in the Groktok omniverse, taught in the sixth age by ascetic duelists who hum at the edge of thought until a rival's focus cracks. Its practitioners project a piercing psychic keening that unravels the will and memory of those who hear it, though the discipline is said to exact a toll from the user's own sanity.

rites.name: Gazhoukturn
rites.text: Gazhoukturn is a churning sky-sea of violet fog that drifts over the frontier worlds of Groktok, its shifting currents tearing ships and cities apart without warning. Old Martial scholars claim the storm breathes in the rhythm of something sleeping far beneath the stars, and every pilot who sails its edges learns to listen for that breath.

rites.name: Kroggar
rites.text: Kroggar is a sprawling fortress-stronghold carved from fused battle-iron in the Groktok frontier, where grox-kings muster their war-hosts before marching into the cold dark. Its gates open onto a pulsing storm-vault that has swallowed whole valleys and sent raiding bands spilling across the stars.

rites.name: Kazhak
rites.text: Kazhak is a sealed resonance in the lattice of the Groktok deep, a standing wave of pressure that bends small tides into slow cathedrals of silt. Its bell-tones are said to hush the spires of the eastern reefs for a full season whenever it wakes.

rites.name: Torournak
rites.text: Torournak is a dampening pulse of ordered static that silences the sorcerous currents of a region, returning its air and stone to plain, honest physics. Champions of the Martial realm wield it to unmake enemy incantations and to wall off battlefields from warping influences. Its reach is bounded by the number of resonant monoliths set in the ground.

rites.name: Kouthaikurn
rites.text: Kouthaikurn is a slow, ashen tide of glassy fallout that wells up from the seams of the Groktok deep-earth when rival martial orders clash their war-engines. Where it passes, stone flows like wax and rivers run backward into their own sources for a season.

rites.name: Grougak
rites.text: Grougak is a sealed lattice of humming glass plates that a Martial-realm warlord can raise over a fleet or citadel to drink incoming force. Each plate darkens as it swallows impact, and once the whole lattice turns black it shatters outward in a shockwave that flattens everything nearby.

rites.name: Vhogaktun
rites.text: Vhogaktun is a self‑propagating nanovirus that hijacks cellular machinery and converts organic matter into inert ash, turning thriving ecosystems into lifeless deserts. Its relentless spread consumes flora, fauna, and even the thin atmosphere, ensuring no trace of vitality remains on any world it touches.

rites.name: Voruzhar
rites.text: Voruzhar is a war-idol of a green-skinned horde whose tusked shape is said to hold two faces that never look the same way. Its devotees claim the ancient tribal chants alone can rouse the surge of roaring charges that sweeps every battlefield it touches.

rites.name: Toruzhaikun
rites.text: Toruzhaikun is a ritual discipline in which the living Gutra-bearers commune with the stored minds of their forebears, drawing counsel from them during the long shifts of a settlement's grim toil. The practice is revered as a shield against forgetfulness and as the reason no clan has ever lost its way in the dark.

rites.name: Khathok
rites.text: In the realm of Zephyrion, the ancient order of Chronokey harnesses the echoes of time, guiding their successors through the labyrinth of history.

rites.name: Vhoggun
rites.text: Vhoggun is a colossal walking fortress that bears an entire society upon its armored shell. Its motion is driven by the synchronized rhythm of ten thousand hearts bound to a central pulse-core. Each thunderous step reshapes the ash plains beneath its striders.

rites.name: Gaizhougar
rites.text: Gaizhougar is a verdant ward-spirit of the Groktok Martial Age, a patron of living growth and the mending of wounds. Her gift is not raw destruction but the quiet renewal of soil, flesh and season alike. Her domain shifts whenever a rival creed tries to rot what she has grown.

rites.name: Groukaigurn
rites.text: Groukaigurn is a concept-level smith-spirit of the Martial realm in Groktok, forging wonders from the sparks of broken oaths during the third age of the Sixth Era. Its anvil-song is said to bind lesser powers into tools that outlast their makers.

rites.name: Draikak
rites.text: Draikak is a spear-wielding war-spirit of the Grokh Wastes, born from a crashed fragment of a sky-fortress and worshipped by drill-sergeants who swear oaths at dawn. Her legend says she shattered her own blade to hold back a flood of ash, and that the pieces still hum beneath the dunes.

rites.name: Karugok
rites.text: Karugok is a weaver-spirit of the Grokt Hollows, who binds the threads of a village's fortune into knotted cord. Her followers, the Knot-Readers, claim to foresee storms by tugging her strands until they sing. She is said to have once unraveled a whole hillside of drought-blighted fields in a single night.

rites.name: Grairnoth
rites.text: Grairnoth is the Ember-Stag of the Thornveil Reaches, a concept of pursuit and wild renewal worshipped by the wanderers who keep the untamed valleys of Groktok. Its favour is said to sharpen a hunter's eye and quicken the paws of beasts that flee before the storm.

rites.name: Drogak
rites.text: Drogak is a concept-deity of the Groktok Martial realm, an unborn power whose coming is foretold by a fringe cult of hunters who believe he will end the reign of the Ecstasy-Lord. Scholars say he exists only as a longing, yet the cult's rites have already scorched three moons' worth of crops in the valleys below.

rites.name: Krazhak
rites.text: Krazhak is a fervent war-faith of the Groktok sky-empires, in which the Tenth Ember of the old Pyre is revered as a living god of endurance. Its clerical orders, the Ashen Conclave, govern the cloud-fortresses and bind every soldier to a vow of unbroken flame. Its rites shape nearly every rank of martial life across the realm.

rites.name: Koukathar
rites.text: Koukathar is a sprawling martial order of verse-singing guardians who keep the old oath-fires burning across the Vaskine marches. Its initiates are trained to channel their sworn resolve into a single devastating strike that can split a fortress wall or quench a rogue storm. Its sanctuaries are said to hold the memory of every battle they have ever won.

rites.name: Vorarnoth
rites.text: Vorarnoth is a sealed lattice of bone-white spires that bends the local sky into a thin doorway, letting travelers step across hundreds of leagues in an instant. Its keepers guard its hidden thresholds on forgotten moons and cracked wastelands, and its gate-song can wake dormant sleepers.

rites.name: Gaithar
rites.text: Gaithar is a codified covenant of martial governance in the realm of Groktok, binding warbands across the Martial sphere into shared rites of command, rotation and reserve. Many war-houses swear to it, though a few hold to older customs and quietly depart from its strictures.

rites.name: Drournok
rites.text: Drournok is a vast dead zone of still, grey void in the heart of the Groktok realm, where the lattice of psychic currents goes silent and no mind can feel beyond its own skull. Ships that enter must crawl on starlight and chronometers, as the old tide-charts are useless here. Its border is marked by drifting wrecks that the Martial clans have claimed as shrines.

rites.name: Vhuggar
rites.text: Vhuggar is a concept of a fractured psychic dimension in the Groktok omniverse, a realm where the emotions of mortals congeal into four rival sovereign territories. Its winds carry memory and appetite, and its shifting seas reflect whatever the dreamers nearby most fear or desire.

rites.name: Torouzhok
rites.text: Torouzhok is a drifting storm of frozen lightning that circles a bruised sky above the Groktok frontier, where iron-clad armies gather to pray to the mirror-faced gods of the deep. Its winds are said to carry the voices of the fallen, and no caravan has crossed its eye in two centuries without losing its compass.

rites.name: Guthurn
rites.text: Guthurn is a drifting sphere of crystallized thunder that hangs above the Groktok ash-fields, humming with a pressure that cracks the sky. Its inhabitants, the Vessel-Singers, channel its rage into weapons that split mountains apart when they are tuned in unison.

rites.name: Gruthogar
rites.text: Gruthogar is a rite of the Grimfang Brotherhood of Groktok, a bloodline-psychic discipline in which a Warden of Ash pulls the ground's own tension into a rent that swallows foes whole. Its practitioners are shunned in the Marrowhold, for the fissure rarely stops where the wielder intended.

rites.name: Thornun
rites.text: Thornun is a battle-hymn woven by the scholar-warriors of Groktok's reading halls, a resonance that lends borrowed strength to a chosen bearer and steadies their limbs against fatigue. Its strongest workings can wrench a fallen wall from its foundations or let a single scholar shrug off a blow that would fell a tower.

rites.name: Thaiktak
rites.text: Thaiktak is a hush-glyph carved into the air by Veilwardens of the Ashen Choir, a silence that drowns the mind-currents of any psyker who steps inside its radius. Choir-sisters raise it around their allies whenever enemy seers begin to hum, so that no vision or curse can take root. Its ring is faintly audible as a low bell that only the unprotected can hear.

rites.name: Vhaizhar
rites.text: Vhaizhar is a psychic discipline of the Groktok Martial realm, taught in the sealed stone cloisters of the seventh age, where adepts learn to push force outward through the mind. Its practitioners, the Hushwardens, strike foes with invisible blows that bruise the air itself before landing. The art is revered for its precision rather than its ruin.

rites.name: Kornar
rites.text: Kornar is a discipline of the Groktok martial orders in which a practitioner folds the perceived rhythm of an opponent's motion into a private, slowed interval. Duelists who master it report that their rivals seem to hang in amber while their own blades keep ordinary pace. Its ceiling is set by how much rhythm a body can hold before the fold tears.

rites.name: Vhurkar
rites.text: Vhurkar is a crimson-veined discipline of the Martial realm, drawn from the dreaming marrow of wandering sparring-monks of Groktok's sixth age. It channels a coiling thread of unstable spirit that can knot a foe's body into new shapes or unravel it entirely.

rites.name: Krogoth
rites.text: Krogoth is a ritual-warping discipline of the Groktok realm, in which a practitioner forces a living body to slough its shape and fuse into a writhing, unstable mass of borrowed flesh. Those who survive the transformation are rarely themselves again, and the pattern is said to spread wherever the ink of the sea-kilns has touched the ground.

rites.name: Grimuktar
rites.text: Grimuktar is a mind-warping discipline practised by the cunning Warp-weavers of the Groktok expanse, who dissolve an opponent's resolve and then bend the foe's own arms against them. Its most celebrated application lets a schemer persuade a fleet's gunners that their cannons face their own decks, and the resulting broadsides can tear apart a sector's worth of worlds in one violent flourish.

rites.name: Gazhokak
rites.text: Gazhokak is a discipline of the Groktok martial realm, taught as a single unbroken motion that ends a contest before the opponent perceives the decision to fight. Its practitioners believe the moment of commitment is the only thing worth measuring, and they train by striking at shadows that have already left their place.

rites.name: Karuggaktar
rites.text: Karuggaktar is a patient hunting doctrine of the Groktok martial orders, in which a warband feigns retreat and lets pursuers wander into prepared killing grounds. Practitioners are taught to wait for weeks, shaping the terrain so that each lure seems an accident.

rites.name: Vhakothar
rites.text: Vhakothar is a discipline of the Martial realm in which practitioners fold their own force into a sealed lattice of slow, wheeling glyphs. Its adepts can briefly release the stored pressure as a single concentrated shove that can flatten a rock formation. Its strongest form is held only for moments before the lattice must be unwound.

rites.name: Gokaigak
rites.text: Gokaigak is a disciplined martial art practiced by ascetic duelists of the Groktok courts, who train to move their bodies through shifting rhythms of breath and tension. Its masters claim to fold the force of a blow into a single held instant, sending it outward long after the strike has landed.

rites.name: Torothar
rites.text: Torothar is a resonant thread of crystallised starlight spun through the dreaming nodes of the Groktok swarm, binding scattered broods into a single listening will. When the thread frays, its bound creatures forget their purpose and fall back to raw hunger and reflex.

rites.name: Vhozhukak
rites.text: Vhozhukak is a concept of Groktok that exists only in the Three Futures, the moment the ending forks and the Library shelves each outcome as a separate volume. It is the ledger of unchosen branches, a quiet idea that makes every possible finish briefly visible before one is kept.

rites.name: Zephiasis
rites.text: Zephiasis is the concept of a single hush that falls between the branching of the Three Futures, when the Library of Groktok shelves each outcome before it is chosen. In the Holy Age of flame and temple orders, its adherents carry it as a discipline of stillness and fire-banked patience.
